name: Amazon MWAA
sku: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow. AWS runs Apache Airflow for the customer; the workflow code is the customer's.

orchestrate.scheduling.note: A managed service for Apache Airflow, an open-source tool used to create, schedule and monitor workflows, run at scale without managing infrastructure.

orchestrate.dependency-dag.note: Workflows are written in Python as Airflow DAGs, stored in an S3 bucket, using the same Airflow user interface and open-source code as Airflow itself.

bands.note: Sets up Airflow, scales workers between limits the customer sets, and patches and upgrades supported Airflow versions periodically.
Airflow logs and metrics go to CloudWatch to spot task delays and workflow errors.
Role-based access to the Airflow web server is defined in IAM policies, and workers assume IAM roles to reach other AWS services.
Each Amazon MWAA environment is a separate Airflow deployment with its own metadata database, so separate environments can hold different stages.

presentation.tagline: Managed Apache Airflow for scheduling and orchestrating pipelines.

cost.note: us-east-1: environment base Small $0.49/hr, Large $0.99/hr (bills all 730hr/month regardless of load, includes 1 worker); additional worker Small $0.055/hr, Large $0.22/hr; additional scheduler/web server (Large) $0.22/$0.11/hr. mw1.medium's own rate was not directly confirmed and is interpolated at $0.74/hr base, $0.11/hr worker (midpoint of small/large) for the 100TB point — worth a direct check against AWS's own pricing table. Each point assumes a plausible environment class and extra-worker count for a pipeline moving that much data.
